messages:
alex: FYI I ran the nightly perf profiler against canary runtime at 2am. Found a surprising token-latency hotspot tied to kernel selection on long-context routes. Summary below.

alex: TL;DR: median token latency up ~12% on /chat-long with nvfuser kernels when sequence > 1024; batching heuristics caused some cross-shard misalignment; KV cache hit-rate fine but eviction thrash increased tail. CSV with traces uploaded to S3: s3://redwood-infer/prof/1759003456/traces.csv

maria: Can you paste the top-level perf numbers? roughs are fine.

alex: Sure. quick paste from the profiler: 
```
route,median_token_latency_ms,95p_token_latency_ms,kv_hit_rate,batch_size_mean,kernel
/chat-short,1.8,5.2,0.98,8,tvm
/chat-long,3.6,23.1,0.93,6,nvfuser
/embeddings,1.4,4.0,0.99,12,tvm
```
Kernel selection policy was choosing nvfuser for long-context models because of peak throughput, but latency penalty on median tokens at smaller batch sizes is real.

sam: Interesting. So kernel choice optimized throughput but hurt token-level latency for small-ish batches. Is the policy using a single global tie-breaker?

alex: Exactly. We have a cost function: score = throughput_factor * 0.7 + mem_usage*0.3, and we pick max score. That favours nvfuser on long sequences. But when requests come in with bursty sizes, the batching heuristic leaves many single-request batches on the fast path and the kernel's per-token overhead dominates.

maria: What about KV cache behavior? you said eviction thrash increased tail. Any numbers?

alex: KV stats show hit-rate stayed >90% but eviction rate doubled during canary window at 02:10-02:30; tie that to smaller batch sizes + more model switches and slower kernel setup time -> more context repopulation. Basically the per-request overlap shrunk and we started rebuilding caches more often.

tara: Could this be from our smart-routing fallback? there were a couple of capacity moves around that time.

alex: There were two route rebalances triggered by autoscaler, yes. It moved a handful of streams between pods and that increased model reloads by ~4x in the window.

sam: For dashboards, we need token-level latency breakdowns (queue / kernel-run / kv-lookup / serialization). Do we already emit those spans?

alex: We emit per-token breakdowns but only at DEBUG level and aggregated into runtime logs. I propose: 1) add structured metrics: token_queue_ms, token_kernel_ms, token_kv_ms, token_serde_ms (tagged by route + kernel_variant) 2) wire them into Flightdeck so per-route KPIs show median/95/99 token latency slices.

maria: Also we need cost-per-token alignment: billing must follow token_kernel_ms + kernel_unit_cost, not endpoint-level p50. Current billing uses total tokens * model_unit which misses kernel selection variation.

tara: Agreed. We should emit kernel_variant dimension in billing events. That lets cost = tokens * unit_cost[kernel_variant, precision]. Also need to track batching discounts (i.e., per-token cost drops with bigger batch_size_mean).

alex: I sketched a proto metric: 
```
metric: token_unit_cost_real_usd
labels: [route, kernel_variant, precision, batch_size_bucket]
value: token_kernel_ms_normalized * kernel_usd_per_ms
```
We can compute nightly unit-econ rolls and feed to billing reconciliation.

sam: Nice. For dashboards: per-route view showing: tokens/sec, median token_kernel_ms, 95p, kv_hit_rate, estimated $/k token (30d avg). Add a small chart for "kernel churn" (fraction of requests switching kernels within a minute) to spot instability.

maria: Who owns the metric exports? eng-runtime produces the spans; eng-platform wires Flightdeck and billing. We need a short plan.

alex: Plan proposal: 
- today: add token-level structured metrics (alex)
- 2d: publish kernel_variant label on billing events (maria)
- 1w: new Flightdeck panels: per-route token slices + $/k token (sam)
- 2w: rollout canary with kernel-selection tweak: prefer lower median_token_latency when batch_size_mean<4 (alex + runtime)

tara: Add tests: simulate small-batch traffic and assert median token latency improvement in staging. Also check KV miss-pressure doesn't regress.

maria: Sounds good. Any quick mitigation while we roll out?

alex: Temp mitigation: change selection tie-breaker to favor tvm for seq>1024 if batch_size_mean<4. I can flip that on canary now.

devops-bot: deploy request queued: change 'kernel_selection_tiebreaker' -> 'favor_tvm_small_batches' to canary namespace. ID: deploy-1759003468

sam: After deploy, can we get 1h heatmap of token_kernel_ms by kernel_variant and route?

alex: Yep. I'll schedule a 1-hour profiler run and pipe results into Flightdeck.

maria: OK all — i'll own billing event schema change. alex/tara/sam coordinate on tests and dashboard widgets. Follow up in #eng-platform tomorrow. :thumbsup:
